title: Content Identity Principle
definition: The principle that each unique and distinct concept within a knowledge system should have a unique, permanent, and machine-parsable identifier.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Think of a library book. Every book has a unique number (its identity) that helps us find, track, and manage it. The Content Identity Principle applies this idea to concepts in our knowledge system.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: The Content Identity Principle is about ensuring that each concept in a knowledge system has a unique, permanent, and machine-parsable identifier (CID). This enables bidirectional mapping, relationship representation, and easy navigation within the knowledge graph.
difficulty_levels.expert: The Content Identity Principle is a foundational concept in knowledge systems and information science. It underpins the design of the CADMIES IPLD system, enabling a rich, interconnected knowledge graph. By assigning a unique CID to each concept, the system enables precise versioning, provenance tracking, and ethical sourcing. The principle also has connections to other fields, such as digital rights management and data integration.

extra_fields.insight: The Content Identity Principle highlights the importance of unique and permanent identification for concepts within a knowledge system, enabling precise navigation, versioning, and ethical sourcing.
